title: Non-blocking follow-ups from backend-ibkr-tickle-keepalive's PR #267 review
description: Non-blocking findings from pr-reviewer's review of PR #267 (backend-ibkr-tickle-keepalive) -- recorded here per CLAUDE.md's 'every non-blocking finding becomes a tracked task' rule so they aren't lost once that PR merges and its review comment scrolls out of view.

checklist.step: docs/architecture/Backend.md §8 step 4 still reads 'not automated by this app today -- a future task ... would need to add that, itself a currently-open gap'. PR #267 is that future task and closed the gap; update that sentence to reflect the keep-alive is now automated via app.main._ibkr_tickle_loop.

Document/test the shutdown-cancellation edge case where lifespan's tickle_task is cancelled while mid-await asyncio.to_thread(provider.tickle) (an HTTP request already dispatched to the worker thread): Task.cancel() can't interrupt an already-running thread-pool work item, so `await tickle_task` in lifespan's finally will block until that in-flight call completes or its httpx client's ~10s timeout elapses before CancelledError actually propagates. Bounded (no leak/crash) but currently untested -- the existing cancellation test only covers cancellation while the task is sleeping.

Widen _ibkr_tickle_loop's except clause from IBKRUnavailableError to a broader Exception (still logging, still not raising). Confirmed via a minimal repro (background code-review pass on PR #267) that today's narrow catch is worse than just 'stops looping': if tickle() ever raised something other than IBKRUnavailableError, the task finishes with that exception stored, tickle_task.cancel() becomes a no-op on an already-done task at shutdown, and `await tickle_task` inside `contextlib.suppress(asyncio.CancelledError)` re-raises the original exception -- propagating out of lifespan()'s own `finally` block and disrupting app shutdown, not just silently pausing the keep-alive. No current code path triggers this (_request's three raise sites are exhaustively IBKRUnavailableError today), so it's latent, not a live bug -- but the fix is cheap and the failure mode is worse than initially scoped.

decisions.decision: Corrected the second checklist item's technical premise: cancelling `tickle_task` while it's mid-`await asyncio.to_thread(provider.tickle)` does NOT block `lifespan()`'s `await tickle_task` until the in-flight call finishes. It returns almost immediately, and the underlying worker thread keeps running the call to completion in the background, orphaned and discarded.
decisions.rationale: Verified with a real-timing repro (both a standalone script and the new `test_shutdown_does_not_block_on_an_in_flight_tickle_call` test in tests/unit/test_main.py, run 10x plus 8x under --cov=app with zero flakes) on Python 3.12.14: `asyncio.to_thread` awaits a plain `asyncio.Future` produced by `loop.run_in_executor` wrapping the executor's `concurrent.futures.Future` via `asyncio.futures._chain_future`. A plain `asyncio.Future.cancel()` (unlike `asyncio.Task.cancel()`) unconditionally marks itself CANCELLED and schedules its callbacks the moment it's called, regardless of whether the underlying thread-pool work is actually interruptible -- it does not wait for `concurrent.futures.Future.cancel()` (which fails silently on an already-running work item) to succeed. So `Task.cancel()` on `tickle_task`, finding it suspended on that wrapped Future, cancels the Future synchronously and `CancelledError` is delivered into the coroutine on the very next event-loop iteration -- not once the thread's blocking call actually returns. The original checklist wording (from a prior 'background code-review pass' finding on PR #267, itself not independently re-verified before being recorded) got this backwards. Documented the corrected behavior inline in app.main.lifespan's finally block and in the new test's docstring rather than silently fixing the checklist wording, per CLAUDE.md's decision-memory rule. This doesn't change the third checklist item's (broadened exception handling) validity -- that finding is unrelated and was independently re-verified as accurate. The second checklist item is still marked done because the actual required work -- 'document/test the shutdown-cancellation edge case' -- was completed correctly against verified behavior, not against the (incorrect) premise as originally phrased.

comments.summary: Independently reproduced and confirmed the PR's central asyncio claim: cancelling a task suspended mid-`await asyncio.to_thread(...)` returns almost immediately rather than blocking on the in-flight thread-pool work, because `asyncio.to_thread` awaits a plain `asyncio.Future` (via `loop.run_in_executor`/`_chain_future`) whose `.cancel()` marks itself cancelled unconditionally, unlike `concurrent.futures.Future.cancel()` on an already-running work item. Verified with a standalone repro (0.1s sleep-then-cancel against a 1.0s worker-thread sleep returned control at ~0.1s, with the worker thread continuing to completion in the background afterward) on the same Python 3.12.14 the repo targets. The task-worker's correction of the original checklist item's (backwards) premise is accurate.

Broadening `_ibkr_tickle_loop`'s catch from `IBKRUnavailableError` to `Exception` (still letting `asyncio.CancelledError`, a `BaseException`, propagate) is a real fix for the latent done-with-exception/no-op-cancel/re-raise-on-shutdown bug described in the PR, and matches an established repo-wide convention for this exact tradeoff (`app/data/stooq_provider.py`, `app/data/yfinance_provider.py` both already use `except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001` with an adjacent justification comment for provider-boundary calls). Unlike the narrower `except DataProviderError`/`except X` used in request-handling code (`app/api/routers/watchlist.py`, `app/api/routers/portfolio.py`) where a loud 500 in tests/CI is the point, this is a background daemon loop whose only job is to keep pinging and not corrupt `lifespan()`'s own shutdown -- the broader catch is the correct choice here, not a downside.

Non-blocking nit (filed as a follow-up task, not blocking this accept): the new comment in `lifespan()`'s `finally` block references the task file at the literal path `docs/tasks/done/backend-ibkr-tickle-keepalive-followups.json`, but at the time this was committed the task's actual state was `testing` (location `docs/tasks/backend-ibkr-tickle-keepalive-followups.json` per `index.json`) -- the comment assumed a not-yet-true `done/` location. It becomes accurate now that this review moves the task to `done/`, but the pattern of hardcoding an assumed future path in a source comment is fragile.

pr_decision.notes: Re-ran full backend suite myself: 1172 passed, 100% line/branch coverage, matching pr-reviewer's numbers exactly. Independently reproduced the asyncio cancellation claim with a standalone script (task cancelled at ~0.15s into a 1.0s worker-thread sleep; await-after-cancel returned in ~0.0001s while the worker thread kept running to completion in the background) -- confirms Task.cancel() on a coroutine suspended in asyncio.to_thread does not block on in-flight thread-pool work. Confirmed FINTRADE_IBKR_ENABLED=false in backend/.env and no live IBKR calls (all new tests mock IBKRProvider). Ran ruff/mypy on the touched files (clean) and skimmed the full diff (main.py, test_main.py, Backend.md, task JSONs, index.json) myself rather than trusting the summary. The decisions entry correcting the checklist's backwards premise is well-documented with a verified rationale; no undecided 'decide X' items.
